newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico jewelry exports seen raised by courier pact.
newsitem.headline: Mexico jewelry exports seen raised by courier pact.

text.p: Jewelry exports from the western Mexican state of Jalisco could be boosted by 30-40 percent in 1996 over last year's $70 million, if safer transportation is arranged, an industry spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.

Exports could be increased by agreements under negotiation with local, domestic and international courier services to transport what is considered a high-risk product, said Roberto Alatorre Rodriguez, chairman of the regional jewelers' and silversmiths' chamber
"At the moment we can't send our products by courier service...it's a problem for marketing and lately they haven't accepted golden jewelry for sending abroad," he said.
Alatorre said he had raised the industry's problems with Mexican Trade Minister Herminio Blanco, who "is going to arrange a meeting for us with the courier services."
